advances: Ordinary simplex roof geometry. The overlap uses a contraction toward a height outside the simplex.

proof:
The normal component of $e$ relative to $\ker v_0$ is $1/\lVert v_0\rVert$, which gives the stated physical measure. Every $t$ section lies in $[-d,1]$ because the other $d$ facet coordinates are at most one and their sum equals $-t$. If $\ell_B$ is the length of the actual $B$ section, with lower endpoint $L_B$, then $0\le\ell_B\le\ell$ and
$$
h+U_B=\ell_B+h+L_B\ge\ell_B+h+L\ge r_e\ell_B
$$
on positive-length columns of $T$. Indeed $h+L>0$. Extend $\ell_B$ by zero elsewhere. The boundary of the full-dimensional transverse projection of $T$ is null, and all its interior columns have positive length by convexity. The pointwise bound $r_e\ell_B\ge\lambda\ell_B-(\lambda-r_e)_+\ell$ and $\int\ell_B\,d\nu=b$ give the dual inequality. Since both endpoints of $F_\lambda([L,U])$ move downward, its overlap with $[L,U]$ has length $[\ell-(h+U)/\lambda]_+$. Integration gives the asserted exact overlap identity.

Put $q_i=(1-v_i\cdot x)/m$, the simplex barycentric coordinates, and $p_i=(v_i\cdot e)_+$. Along a chord, for $p_i>0$ we have $q_i(L)=q_i(U)+p_i\ell/m$. Summing these and retaining $q_0(U)=(1-U)/m$ shows $\sigma\ell\le d+U$. Hence $r_e\ge \sigma(h+U)/(d+U)\ge\sigma\beta$, using $h>d$ and $U\le1$. This gives the zero-volume range.

For $\lambda>\sigma\beta$ put $a=1/(\lambda-1)$. The inverse of $F_\lambda$ adds $a(t+h)e$. Since $t+h>0$ on $T$, only facets with $p_i>0$ give additional constraints, and these are $q_i+a p_iq_0-a p_i\beta\ge0$. Set $\mu_i=q_i+a p_iq_0-a p_i\beta$. Then
$$
q_0=\frac{\mu_0+a\beta}{1+a},\qquad
(1-\sigma/\lambda)\mu_0+\sum_{i\ne0}\mu_i=1-\sigma\beta/\lambda.
$$
Conversely a nonnegative solution reconstructs original $q_i\ge0$: it has $\mu_0\le(\lambda-\sigma\beta)/(\lambda-\sigma)<1<\beta$, so $q_0<\beta$ and $q_i=\mu_i+a p_i(\beta-q_0)\ge0$. The barycentric sum is one by the displayed linear identity. Thus in independent coordinates $\mu_i$, $i\ne0$, the overlap is a standard simplex of scale $1-\sigma\beta/\lambda$. The determinant of the independent $q$-to-$\mu$ map is $1-a(\sigma-1)=(\lambda-\sigma)/(\lambda-1)>0$ by the rank-one determinant identity. Relative to $|T|$, this gives the claimed overlap volume.

When $\sigma=1$ this is $V(1-\beta/\lambda)^d$. For $\sigma>1$ and $\beta<\lambda\le\sigma\beta$ the comparison is strict by the zero-volume formula. For $\lambda>\sigma\beta$, set $x=(\sigma-1)/(\lambda-1)$ and $c=\beta(\lambda-1)/(\lambda-\beta)$. The ratio to the $\sigma=1$ formula is $(1-cx)^d/(1-x)<1$ because $c>1$ and $0<x<cx<1$.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $m=d+1$, and $T=\{x:v_i\cdot x\le1,\ 0\le i\le d\}$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$ with spanning normals satisfying $\sum_i v_i=0$. Fix $e$ with $v_0\cdot e=1$ and write $x=y+te$ with $t=v_0\cdot x$, $y\in\ker v_0$. Use $\pi_e x=y$ and $d\nu=d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\lVert v_0\rVert$. For $h>d$, set $H=h+1$, $\beta=H/m$, and $\sigma=\sum_i(v_i\cdot e)_+$. For a convex body $B\subseteq T$ of volume $b$, write $U_B(y)$ for its upper $t$ endpoint and $R_e(B,h)=\int_{\pi_e B}(h+U_B)\,d\nu$.

Write $[L,U]$ for the $t$ section of $T$, $\ell=U-L$ for its length and $r_e=(h+U)/\ell$ on positive-length sections. For $\lambda>1$ let $F_\lambda(y+te)=y+[t-(t+h)/\lambda]e$ and $W(\lambda)=|T\cap F_\lambda(T)|$. Then
$$
R_e(B,h)\ge\lambda b-\int(\lambda-r_e)_+\ell\,d\nu
=\lambda[b-W(\lambda)] .
$$
The overlap has volume zero when $\lambda\le\sigma\beta$. Otherwise
$$
W(\lambda)=V\,\frac{\lambda-1}{\lambda-\sigma}\left(1-\frac{\sigma\beta}{\lambda}\right)^d .
$$
For $\lambda>\beta$ one has $W(\lambda)\le V(1-\beta/\lambda)^d$, strictly when $\sigma>1$.
title: Exact affine overlap for simplex roof costs
